title: Two dads, one childhood dream, and a little cosmic pet we built for our kids ❤
author: MahereMarley
selftext:
**Hey everyone!**

A colleague and I are both dads, and for the past months we’ve been working on something that started as a little nostalgic idea and somehow turned into a full-blown indie game.

We both grew up with Tamagotchis. We remember checking on our little virtual pets, feeding them, playing with them, watching them grow, and getting weirdly attached to a bunch of pixels on a tiny screen.

Now that we have kids of our own, we thought it would be amazing to bring a little bit of that magic back. Something our kids could enjoy, but that would also make people our age feel a little nostalgic.

So we decided to build our own virtual pet.

It’s called **Lumino – Cosmic Pet**.

The idea is simple: you hatch a tiny creature made of starlight, give it a name, and take care of it. Feed it, cuddle it, play with it, dress it up, decorate its little room and watch it grow through different evolution stages.

But we didn’t want it to feel like just another virtual pet app.

We wanted to create something genuinely cozy. Something you open when you want to relax, smile a little and spend a few minutes with your little cosmic friend.

We put an almost ridiculous amount of attention into the little details. Especially the sounds.

My colleague has some experience with sound design, so he took care of a lot of that side of things. We spent a lot of time making sure every little interaction had its own sound, reaction and personality.

Petting Lumino, tickling it, feeding it, playing with it… all those tiny moments needed to feel right. We really wanted Lumino to feel alive rather than just like a collection of animations.

**A little about how we built it:**

We’re a team of two, and AI played a huge role in making this project possible.

We used Claude, mainly Opus (4.8 through 5.5), throughout development.

It helped us turn ideas into reality much faster than we could have managed otherwise. But there was still a ridiculous amount of planning, testing, tweaking, fixing and arguing over tiny details involved haha

We’re both dads, so finding time to work on a project like this wasn’t always easy. There were plenty of late nights and moments where we wondered whether we were completely crazy for taking this on.

But seeing our own kids enjoy something we built ourselves made it worth it.

**Now comes the part I honestly didn’t expect.**

We launched Lumino about two weeks ago, and we’re slowly getting our first players and feedback.

Some of the feedback has been incredibly heartwarming.

We’ve had people with disabilities try the game, and some of them told us how much they loved it. One of the players was blind and actually played Lumino using VoiceOver. He also took the time to give us feedback.

I can’t really describe how much that meant to both of us.

We never expected this little project, which originally started because we wanted to recreate some childhood nostalgia for our own kids, to connect with people in ways like this.

It honestly made us believe even more in what we’re building.

It also reminded us why we wanted to make Lumino in the first place: to create something that makes people feel good. Something warm, gentle and welcoming.

**Of course, we’re still very early.**

There are so many things we’d love to improve, add and explore. We’re listening to feedback and want to keep making Lumino better.

I’m sharing this here because I’d love to hear what you think.

Does Lumino bring back any Tamagotchi memories for you? What would you like to see in a modern virtual pet game? And if you try it, please tell us what you think, even if it’s critical.

We’re two dads who decided to build something we wished existed for our kids, and now we’re just incredibly happy that other people are enjoying it too.

If you’d like to give our little cosmic pet a home, here’s the link:

[https://apps.apple.com/de/app/lumino-cosmic-pet/id6818081961](https://apps.apple.com/de/app/lumino-cosmic-pet/id6818081961)

Thanks for reading, and thanks to everyone who supports small indie projects like ours. It genuinely means a lot.

**– The Lumino team ❤**️
